note: BOW's canonical concept taxonomy. It was NOT invented for the Library — it is a crosswalk over the four concept vocabularies that already existed independently across BOW products. Every concept records where it is attested. `crosswalk` lets each product keep its own internal ids while the Library speaks one language.

website-concept-map.shape: 30 entries, ids cm-01..cm-30, categories micro | macro | sports_specific, each mapped to a Track 101 or 201 module
website-concept-map.role: BOW's public, curated Economics spine. Adopted as the backbone of the canonical taxonomy.

website-glossary.shape: ~42 terms, categories cap_mechanics | economics | analytics | business
website-glossary.role: Student-facing vocabulary. Used here as an alias source, not as a separate concept layer.

highway-world-curriculum.role: Decision-economics and sports-business vocabulary that the website spine does not cover. Folded in.

decision-challenges-blueprint.shape: 6 weighted concepts C1..C6 with micro-skill ids, mapped to NYSED Personal Finance objectives
decision-challenges-blueprint.role: The only Financial Literacy vocabulary in the account. Adopted wholesale as the FinLit spine.

pillars.economics: BOW Economics. Backbone: the website concept map.
pillars.financial-literacy: BOW Financial Literacy. Backbone: the Decision Challenges blueprint.

concepts.name: Opportunity Cost
concepts.definition: The value of the best alternative given up when a choice is made.

concepts.name: Scarcity
concepts.definition: Limited resources force ranking and choice; not everything can be had at once.

concepts.name: Incentives
concepts.definition: Rewards and penalties that change how people behave.

concepts.name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
concepts.definition: Weighing expected gain against total cost before committing.

concepts.name: Tradeoffs
concepts.definition: Gaining on one dimension while giving up on another; no option is free.

concepts.name: Expected Value
concepts.definition: The average outcome of a decision weighted by how likely each result is.

concepts.name: Risk and Reward
concepts.definition: Higher potential payoff usually carries higher chance of loss.

concepts.name: Uncertainty
concepts.definition: Deciding well when the outcome genuinely cannot be known in advance.

concepts.name: Sunk Cost
concepts.definition: Money already spent that should not influence the next decision.

concepts.name: Marginal Value
concepts.definition: What one more unit is actually worth, which is rarely what the average is worth.

concepts.name: Law of Demand
concepts.definition: As price rises, quantity demanded generally falls.

concepts.name: Law of Supply
concepts.definition: As price rises, quantity supplied generally rises.

concepts.name: Market Equilibrium
concepts.definition: The price at which what buyers want matches what sellers offer.

concepts.name: Price Elasticity
concepts.definition: How sharply demand responds when price moves.

concepts.name: Pricing Strategy
concepts.definition: Choosing a price to hit a goal — fill the building, maximise revenue, or protect the brand.

concepts.name: Revenue Management
concepts.definition: Managing inventory and price together to get the most from limited capacity.

concepts.name: Competition & Market Structure
concepts.definition: How many sellers there are, and what that does to price and choice.

concepts.name: Monopoly
concepts.definition: A single seller with the power to set price.

concepts.name: Market Inefficiency
concepts.definition: Mispricing that a sharper buyer can exploit.

concepts.name: Comparative Advantage
concepts.definition: Doing what you give up least to do, and trading for the rest.

concepts.name: Supply Chain
concepts.definition: The chain of steps that gets a good from source to customer, and what happens when a link breaks.

concepts.name: Externalities
concepts.definition: Costs or benefits that land on people outside the deal.

concepts.name: Public Goods
concepts.definition: Things everyone can use and no one can be kept out of, which markets underprovide.

concepts.name: Market Failure
concepts.definition: When a market on its own produces a bad outcome.

concepts.name: Fiscal Policy
concepts.definition: Government taxing and spending to steer the economy.

concepts.name: Monetary Policy
concepts.definition: Central-bank control of money and interest rates.

concepts.name: GDP & Economic Growth
concepts.definition: The total value an economy produces, and why it rises or falls.

concepts.name: Inflation
concepts.definition: A general rise in prices that shrinks what a dollar buys.

concepts.name: The Business Cycle
concepts.definition: The repeating swing between expansion and downturn.

concepts.name: The Multiplier Effect
concepts.definition: One dollar of spending circulating into more than one dollar of activity.

concepts.name: Salary Cap
concepts.definition: A hard limit on total payroll that forces every signing to be a choice.

concepts.name: Luxury Tax
concepts.definition: A penalty payment for spending above a threshold.

concepts.name: Bird Rights
concepts.definition: An exception letting a team re-sign its own player above the cap.

concepts.name: Mid-Level Exception
concepts.definition: A fixed allowance to sign a player without cap room.

concepts.name: Revenue Sharing
concepts.definition: Pooling league income so smaller markets stay viable.

concepts.name: Market Size
concepts.definition: How the size of a team's city changes what it can earn and pay.

concepts.name: Media Rights
concepts.definition: Selling the right to broadcast games — often the largest revenue line.

concepts.name: Analytics & WAR
concepts.definition: Using measured contribution rather than reputation to value a player.

concepts.name: Surplus Value
concepts.definition: Production received above what was paid for it.

concepts.name: Roster Windows
concepts.definition: The limited stretch in which a roster can realistically contend.

concepts.name: Pick Value & Decay
concepts.definition: What a draft pick is worth and how fast that worth drops down the board.

concepts.name: Asset Valuation
concepts.definition: Putting a defensible number on what something is worth.

concepts.name: Roster Construction
concepts.definition: Assembling a whole team under a constraint rather than collecting good parts.

concepts.name: Fan Engagement
concepts.definition: Winning and keeping the attention of the people who pay.

concepts.name: Customer Segmentation
concepts.definition: Different buyers want different things and will pay differently.

concepts.name: Sponsorship & Brand Fit
concepts.definition: What a partnership is worth, and what the wrong partner costs.

concepts.name: Operations Tradeoffs
concepts.definition: Running the day-to-day under real constraints of time, staff and space.

concepts.name: Negotiation
concepts.definition: Reaching a deal both sides will sign.

concepts.name: BATNA
concepts.definition: Your best move if the deal falls through — the thing that sets your walk-away.

concepts.name: Leverage
concepts.definition: Who needs the deal more, and what that is worth.

concepts.name: Auctions & Bidding
concepts.definition: Competing bids reveal what something is worth — and tempt overpaying.

concepts.name: Principal-Agent
concepts.definition: When the person acting for you wants something different from what you want.

concepts.name: Stakeholder Management
concepts.definition: Balancing parties who want incompatible things from the same decision.

concepts.name: Crisis Management
concepts.definition: Deciding under time pressure when information is incomplete and public.

concepts.name: Reputation Risk
concepts.definition: Damage to standing that no balance sheet shows until later.

concepts.name: Entrepreneurship
concepts.definition: Starting and growing a venture under real constraints and real risk.

concepts.name: Capital & Investment
concepts.definition: Putting money to work now for a larger, uncertain return later.

concepts.name: Portfolio Thinking
concepts.definition: Judging a set of bets together rather than one at a time.

concepts.name: Optionality
concepts.definition: Keeping future choices open, and what that flexibility is worth.

concepts.name: Time Horizon
concepts.definition: Trading a gain now against a larger gain later.

concepts.name: Leadership Under Constraints
concepts.definition: Owning a call, and its consequences, when every option costs something.

concepts.name: Signal vs Noise
concepts.definition: Telling real information from randomness before acting on it.

concepts.name: Process vs Results
concepts.definition: A good decision can lose and a bad one can win; judge the reasoning, not just the scoreboard.

concepts.name: Model Risk & False Confidence
concepts.definition: A number from a model is still a guess; over-trusting it is its own risk.

concepts.name: Use Income by Reliability
concepts.definition: Distinguish dependable money from money that depends on a condition.

concepts.name: Calculate and Compare Full Cost
concepts.definition: Combine recurring and one-time costs across the whole planning period.

concepts.name: Construct a Viable Budget
concepts.definition: Give every available dollar one clear job without overcommitting.

concepts.name: Build an Executable Contingency
concepts.definition: Create a lower-resource fallback using only money that can still move.

concepts.name: Adapt After Conditions Change
concepts.definition: Use new information, preserve commitments, and reconcile the revised plan.

concepts.name: Defend a Financial Strategy
concepts.definition: Explain workability, priority, and opportunity cost using the relevant numbers.

concepts.name: Saving Toward a Goal
concepts.definition: Setting money aside on purpose to reach something later.

gapsAcknowledged: The Financial Literacy spine has 7 concepts against 64 Economics concepts. That imbalance is real: it reflects BOW's actual portfolio, not a modelling shortcut.

Credit, debt, interest, and insurance appear in BOW's source vocabulary but no discovered simulation teaches them as a primary concept, so they are deliberately NOT listed as canonical concepts yet. Adding a concept no BOW experience teaches would create a phantom gap rather than an honest one.

Concepts marked attestedIn: product-source are drawn from discovered simulation titles and source vocabulary rather than an existing BOW taxonomy file. They are the taxonomy's newest and least settled members.
